To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the relations of central hemodynamics with cardiac dimensions and systolic function are complex, and that the relations of CFPWV and central pulse pressure to LV diastole are independent of each other and of MAP.

the differing relations of steady (mean arterial pressure) and pulsatile (pulse pressure) components of central blood pressure and aortic stiffness (pulse wave velocity) with left ventricular dimensions and function have been clarified.

central hemodynamics and car­ otid-femoral pulse wave veloc­ ity are conjointly but variably related to left ventricular struc­ ture, that carotid-femoral pu­lse wave velocity is inversely related to left ventric­ular diastolic func­ tion, and that central pulse pressure is positively related to left ventri­ cular systolic func­ tion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationships of central blood pressure and aortic stiffness (a measure of aortic wall stiffness) to left ventricular ( LV) structure and function.
the relationships of central hemodynamic and aortic stiffness measurements with left ventricular ( LV) structure and function.
the relationships of aortic stiffness and central blood pressure to the structure and function of the left ventricle (LV).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the relations of steady and pulsatil components of central pressure and aortic stiffness are complex and variable and that additional studies are needed to further clarify these relations.

the relations of central hemodynamics to cardiac structure and function are complex, and the differing relations of central steady and pulsatile pressures and aortic stiffness to cardiac dimensions and function need to be considered when interpreting these associations.
aortic stiffness is associated with LV structure but not with systolic function, whereas both the steady and pulsatile hemodynamic components are associated with systolic and diastic function.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
central blood pressure is related to LV size and function.

aortic stiffness is associated with diastolic dysfunction but not systolic function and that the steady component of central hemodynamics, mean arterial pressure, is associated with LV hypertrophy but not with LV diastole.
the steady and pulsatile hemodynamic components are related to LV structure and function in a different manner.
The main takeaway from our work is that
aortic stiffness is not associated with left ventricular (heart muscle) structure.
the steady and pulsatile elements of central pressure have different relations to left ventricular structure and function.
the steady and pulsatile hemodynamic components are differentially associated with cardiac function and structure.
